'''She-crab soup''' is a rich [[soup]], similar to [[bisque (food)|bisque]], made of [[milk]] or [[heavy cream]], [[Crab meat|crab]] or [[Fish stock (food)|fish stock]], [[Callinectes sapidus|Atlantic blue crab]] meat, and (traditionally) crab [[roe]], and a small amount of dry [[sherry]] added as it is plated. It may be thickened either by heat reduction or with a [[purée]] of boiled [[rice]]; it may also include such seasonings as [[Mace (spice)|mace]] and [[shallots]] or [[onions]].  The soup is a regional specialty from the [[South Carolina Lowcountry]].  It is commonly featured on the menus of many [[Charleston, South Carolina]], and [[Savannah, Georgia]] [[restaurants]].<ref>Levitas, Gloria (June 27, 1982). [https://www.nytimes.com/1982/06/27/travel/fare-of-the-country-she-crab-soup-southern-tradition.html?pagewanted=all "She-Crab Soup: Southern Tradition"], ''New York Times''. Retrieved November 1, 2015.</ref><ref>Scott Hurst, Andrea. [http://www.southernliving.com/food/entertaining/crab-soup "She-Crab Soup"], ''Southern Living''. Retrieved November 1, 2015.</ref><ref>[http://whatscookingamerica.net/History/Chowder/SheCrabSoup.htm "She-Crab Soup Recipe and History"], What's Cooking America. Retrieved November 1, 2015.</ref>

The soup is named for the "she-crab", or female crab, originally a [[Gravidity and parity#Gravidity in biology|gravid]] (roe-carrying) crab, as the orange crab roe comprise a chief ingredient in traditional she-crab soup.  As with [[turtle soup]], other ingredients may be added to the soup or substituted for others, although crab meat is found in all versions.

Regulations in Maryland and other states restrict the collection of egg-bearing female crabs.<ref>{{cite web |title=State of Maryland regulations 08.02.03.08 |url=http://www.dsd.state.md.us/comar/comarhtml/08/08.02.03.08.htm |website=Maryland Division of State Documents |publisher=State of Maryland |access-date=25 July 2022}}</ref>
